themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (likely Uber/Lyft) spiked dramatically to 24 complaints last week versus a baseline of 2.0 per week—a 1100% increase—suggesting a sudden surge in traffic congestion, illegal parking, or passenger behavior issues in Washington Heights/Inwood this past week.
evidence: 24 for-hire vehicle complaints last week vs. 2.0 weekly average over 8 weeks (1100% spike, z-score: 15.56)
Highest statistical severity among all spikes this reporting period
No prior news coverage or community board documentation of this issue
reporting_angles: Interview residents and business owners about congestion and traffic patterns; determine if this reflects a new app promotion, influx of out-of-state drivers, or enforcement gap
Map complaint locations to identify specific corridors (e.g., near subway hubs, commercial strips) experiencing the worst impact

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Deterioration Spike
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 18 this week compared to a 3.8 weekly average—a 380% increase (z-score: 9.13)—indicating a sudden, localized wave of potholes, cracks, or tripping hazards that could signal deferred street maintenance or accelerated wear in specific neighborhoods.
evidence: 18 sidewalk condition complaints this week vs. 3.8 weekly average (380% spike, z-score: 9.13)
Community board has repeatedly requested litter basket collection and park/street upgrades, suggesting underlying sanitation and maintenance gaps
Street Condition (618 complaints over 90 days) remains in top 10 overall complaint types
reporting_angles: Conduct a ground tour of high-complaint blocks; photograph affected areas and assess whether this is concentrated in one neighborhood or distributed across Washington Heights and Inwood
Interview DOT officials about repair backlogs and seasonal maintenance schedules; cross-check against permit filings showing 366 building alterations

themes_detail.label: Encampment Expansion
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints surged to 8 this week from a baseline of 1.4 per week—a 482% increase (z-score: 4.43)—suggesting a rapid increase in homelessness or public-space occupation in a district where Community Board has long requested enhanced park safety and security staffing.
evidence: 8 encampment complaints this week vs. 1.4 weekly average (482% spike, z-score: 4.43)
Community Board has filed recurring budget requests for park safety and enhanced security staff, indicating this is a longstanding, worsening concern
Food Poisoning (4 complaints this week, 300% spike) and Unsanitary Condition (1,334 over 90 days, top 5) may be related to encampment-linked conditions
reporting_angles: Locate and interview affected residents and business owners about encampment sites, timeline of occupation, and any service outreach; map correlations with park locations
Investigate city resources: Has NYC deployed additional outreach teams? What is the status of shelter capacity in or near Washington Heights/Inwood?

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints jumped to 4 this week from a 1.0 weekly baseline—a 300% spike (z-score: 4.24)—raising questions about a localized foodborne illness outbreak or a cluster of unsanitary restaurant/food vendor conditions this week.
evidence: 4 food poisoning complaints this week vs. 1.0 weekly average (300% spike, z-score: 4.24)
Unsanitary Condition (1,334 complaints over 90 days) is top 5 overall, suggesting poor sanitation culture or overcrowding in food facilities
No recent news or Reddit discussion documenting this outbreak
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health; request inspection records and complaint details for the past 7–10 days to identify common restaurants, vendors, or neighborhoods
Interview affected residents about symptoms, timing, and location of illness; determine if cases cluster around a specific establishment or food type

themes_detail.label: Public Hygiene & Sanitation Concerns
themes_detail.summary: Three related spikes converge this week: Urinating in Public (3 complaints vs. 0.2 baseline, 1100% spike), Industrial Waste (3 vs. 0.2 baseline, 1100% spike), and Encampment (8 vs. 1.4 baseline, 482% spike)—suggesting a deterioration in street-level cleanliness and public space management that aligns with long-standing community board requests for more frequent litter collection.
evidence: Urinating in Public: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 4.16)
Industrial Waste: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 4.16)
Community Board recurring request: 'Provide more frequent litter basket collection' (Agency: Department of Sanitation)
Unsanitary Condition remains in top 5 complaint categories (1,334 over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Map the three spikes (urinating, industrial waste, encampments) geographically to determine if they cluster in specific zones (e.g., subway stations, waterfront, commercial strips)
Interview Sanitation and Parks officials about collection schedules, staffing, and enforcement in Washington Heights/Inwood; compare resource allocation to other NYC neighborhoods
